pageCache.pageTitle: New Reception Starters | St Andrew's CE Primary School – Yetminster
pageCache.text:
New Reception Starters
At St Andrew’s, we understand that choosing the right school for your child is a big decision. We are delighted that you are considering us for this exciting new chapter in your child’s life. As you prepare for this important step, we’d love to tell you more about what makes our school special and how we can help your child thrive.
Why Choose St Andrew’s?
A Warm and Nurturing Environment
At St Andrew’s, we believe that every child deserves a safe, supportive space where they can develop their love for learning. Our experienced and dedicated teachers are committed to nurturing each child’s unique potential, ensuring they grow in confidence and curiosity every day.
Forest School Program
We’re proud to offer a rich Forest School program that allows children to learn and explore in a natural, outdoor setting. Through this hands-on approach, they develop independence, problem-solving skills, and a deep appreciation for the environment.
Active PTFA (Parent, Teacher, and Friends Association)
Our PTFA is a vibrant part of school life, organising fun events and activities that bring families together and enrich the school experience. It’s a fantastic way to get involved, meet new people, and support the school.
Preparing Your Child for School
Starting school is a major milestone, and it’s normal for children and parents to feel both excited and a little nervous. To help your child feel ready and confident, here are a few tips to focus on over the next few months:
School Readiness Tips
Independent Toileting
Help your child feel confident in using the toilet by themselves and washing their hands afterwards. This is an essential skill for their independence in school.
Eating with Cutlery
Practise using cutlery at home so your child can manage mealtimes independently. This will help them feel confident and comfortable during lunchtime.
Dressing Themselves
Encourage your child to put on their coat and shoes, and practise doing up zips and buttons. Dressing independently boosts their self-esteem and sense of achievement.
Recognising Their Own Name
Being able to recognise their name, especially on clothing or personal items, helps children feel more organised and responsible for their belongings.
Excitement for School
Most importantly, foster a sense of excitement! Encourage your child to look forward to school by talking about all the fun activities they will do and the new friends they’ll meet. Your positivity will help them feel excited and reassured.

Governance
Academy Committees
The Academy Committees (ACs) support the Trustees to fulfil their responsibility for oversight of each school within the Trust, acting as the eyes and ears of the Board at local level. Their role is more focused than that of a traditional school governing body. The SAST central team manages – finance, HR, Estates, IT, and others.
The ACs responsibility is to monitor and scrutinise teaching and learning, welfare, and safeguarding issues. The ACs provide challenge and support to the Headteachers and senior leadership team, and represent the Trust to local stakeholders – parents, students, staff and the community. Two representatives of each AC are elected from among that school’s parents, while a further representative will be elected by the staff. The Headteacher is ex officio. The remaining representatives are appointed by the Trustees following recommendation from the AC and Headteacher, based on skills and experience, or in our Church of England academies, the Diocese of Salisbury and the Diocese of Bath & Wells receive and consider nominations and appoint. Ex ‘VA’ schools must have a majority of foundation representatives and ex ‘VC’ 25% of representatives must be foundation. Each AR is appointed for a term of four years, after which time, AC representatives, with agreement from the Diocese or Trustees, may agree to renewal of further term(s).
The AC will meet at the beginning of each full term (three times a year), plus an additional meeting to review published exam performance. Typically, this additional meeting will take place during the summer term for primary schools, once the SATS results have been published, whereas for secondary schools, this meeting will take place during the autumn term

Special Educational Needs

Telphone: 01935 872430
To discuss your child’s individual needs please email Miss Wood directly or call the office to make an appointment.
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities at St Andrew’s
All children are valued, respected and welcomed to the school whatever their additional educational need. We will support their learning and ensure they are fully included in all school activities, making full use of externally provided facilities where appropriate.
We are well equipped to meet the needs of all children who come to St Andrew’s. We identify children with additional needs at an early stage and have an experienced Special Educational Needs Coordinator, Becky Wood who is skilled at providing extra support for those who need it.
Becky and the class teacher will work together to create a Support Plan that will meet the needs of specific children. You will have the opportunity to meet with Becky and your child’s class teacher regularly to discuss their progress.
We also work closely with outside agencies and professionals who can offer advice and support such as: Educational Psychology Service, Speech Therapists, Educational Welfare Service, Hearing Impairment Service, Family Partnership Zone and Social Care Services. A copy of the Special Needs Policy is attached above.
Click here for information about the local offer. All local authorities must now develop and publish their Local Offer to explain what is available for children and young people with SEN and disabilities across education, health and social care.
Emotional and Mental Health
At St Andrew’s, we place great importance on the emotional health and well-being of our pupils. We are fortunate to have a qualified counsellor from Little Lives who visits the school weekly, and Mrs Shortman, our trained Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA), runs regular sessions to support children’s emotional development. As a Trauma-Informed School, with Mrs Hedges holding a Level 5 diploma, we are committed to understanding and addressing the social and emotional needs of our pupils.
We recognise that emotional health is closely linked to learning and overall development, as highlighted in the Children Act 2004 (Every Child Matters), and we ensure that our approach supports the all-round growth of every child.
Individual needs
All children should be nurtured in accordance with their individual needs. There will always be children and young people in schools facing life challenges that detract from their ability to engage with learning, and some will require greater support to increase their emotional literacy than others.

Physical Education
We offer a rich and varied PE programme to help children develop skills, fitness, and a love of physical activity. Lessons are delivered by a mix of class teachers and external coaches from Premier Education, giving pupils the opportunity to experience a wide range of sports and activities.
We also offer a variety of sports-based after-school clubs, providing even more opportunities for children to be active, try new sports, and have fun.
When does my child have PE?

Wednesday – Willow and Oak

Send your child to school dressed in school PE kit every day they have a planned PE session.
Forest School
At St Andrew’s, our Forest School sessions take place mostly off-site at Vecklands Woods and are led by trained Forest School teachers from Lower Covey. During these full-day sessions, children enjoy outdoor learning experiences such as cooking over a fire, building dens, creating seasonal forest crafts, and exploring the woods. Each class attends Forest School every Monday, so pupils typically experience a full Forest School day roughly once a month, giving them the chance to connect with nature, develop practical skills, and enjoy active, hands-on learning.

At lunchtimes we have lunch time clubs which can include Chess and Recorder
After school clubs tend to vary during the year but popular ones are gardening, art, Lego and performing arts,
Our children really enjoy all of these clubs and they can give them a different perspective on life and another opportunity in which to blossom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Foundational knowledge | St Andrew's CE Primary School – Yetminster
pageCache.text:
Foundational knowledge
Foundational knowledge approach at St Andrew’s
At St Andrew’s Primary School, our aim is to create strong foundations for every child, enabling them to grow in confidence and build upon these foundations as they continue their educational journey.
Strong Foundations refers to guidance published by the Department for Education and Ofsted that highlights the importance of making sure every child in the early years and early primary stages (Reception and Key Stage 1) builds the essential knowledge and skills they need to thrive throughout their whole school life.
At its heart, this means:
Securing the Basics Early
It’s about ensuring that children have a really strong grounding in the fundamentals — such as communication, early reading and phonics, writing, maths, and social and physical development — before they are asked to do more complex tasks. Children need repeated practice and teaching of core skills so that they remember and can confidently use them later on.
A Clear and Coherent Curriculum
Schools should be clear about what children need to learn and when, and make sure learning is sequenced properly so that each new step builds carefully on what came before. Children benefit most when learning is structured, well-planned, and matched to their developmental stage.
Focus on Fluency and Mastery
Rather than rushing into more challenging work, children are supported to become fluent — that is, comfortable and confident — in key skills like reading, writing and number work before they move on. This supports confidence, later learning and enjoyment of school.
Helping All Children Succeed
The guidance highlights that strong foundations are especially important for children who start school with lower levels of knowledge or confidence, or who have had limited early learning opportunities. The aim is for every child to have the solid building blocks they need so they’re ready for the rest of their education.
So, when we talk about Strong Foundations at school, we mean:
✅ Teaching and reinforcing the basics in a way that makes sense to young learners ✅ Making sure children have lots of opportunities to practice and become confident ✅ Helping children feel successful and ready for future learning ✅ Planning learning carefully so each step fits with what children already know
This is not about “teaching to a test” — it’s about giving children a really solid start that helps them feel confident, curious and capable as they continue through school.
Please see below for further information on how we aim to embed foundational knowledge and skills here at St Andrew’s (Yetminster).
Oracy
Handwriting
At St Andrew’s, we follow Unlocking Letters and Sounds for handwriting. Good handwriting is critical to children’s writing progress. It is essential that handwriting is practised until it is fluent and effortless so that the children can put all their effort into thinking about what they are writing.
Unlocking Handwriting Progression Unlocking Handwriting is a whole school handwriting programme. The progression used in Unlocking Handwriting follows the National Curriculum progression, with some additional content included based upon a wealth of experience of teaching handwriting in schools, feedback from schools seeking a comprehensive, progressive handwriting programme and updated guidance(including requirements from the National Curriculum).The progression Is structured broadly in units which are broken down into multiple sessions, offering a clear focus for each discrete handwriting lesson. Similar to the structure of Unlocking Letters and Sounds, Unlocking Handwriting provides ‘Mastery’ units for children to embed and secure the knowledge they have previously learnt. The programme also provides frequent opportunities for children to revisit previous learning and embed this before further refining their handwriting skills. Pupil Premium and P.E Funding
Nothing is impossible with God. Luke 1:37
P.E Funding 2025-2026
We receive PE and Sport Premium funding to enhance our physical education provision and promote healthy, active lifestyles. This funding allows us to provide high-quality lessons, employ specialist coaches, offer a wider range of sports, and run extra-curricular clubs and activities. We use the funding strategically to ensure that all pupils have opportunities to develop skills, confidence, and a love of physical activity.
Please see below how we spend this funding:
2025-2026 submission
Pupil Premium Funding
The Pupil Premium is additional funding provided to schools on top of the main school budget. It is allocated based on the number of pupils on roll who have been eligible for free school meals (FSM) within the last six years. Pupil Premium funding is also provided for children from service families and pupils who are ‘Looked After’ (in care) or adopted. Families can check eligibility and apply for Free School Meals here: Dorset Council – Free School Meals.
Schools decide how the Pupil Premium is spent, as they are best placed to assess the additional support needed for individual pupils. Schools are held accountable for how they use this funding to help pupils from low-income families achieve their full potential.
At St Andrew’s, our Pupil Premium lead is Mrs Anna Hedges, who works closely with staff across the school to ensure that this funding is used effectively to support the learning and well-being of our Pupil Premium children. You can view our full Pupil Premium Strategy here: Pupil Premium Strategy

Pupil Healthcare
Nothing is impossible with God. Luke 1:37
We maintain a high standard of first aid and health and safety training amongst our staff. All classes and areas have regularly checked first aid boxes and a more substantive supply of first aid is kept with the school’s nominated first aider in the school office. We will alert parents to head bumps by email or if are concerned your child needs monitoring at home or elsewhere will contact you immediately.
If your child needs to take prescribed medicine during the school day, it can be left at the school office where it will be stored in appropriate conditions and administered at the required time. We are also happy to hold over-the-counter medication, such as hayfever relief or Calpol-type pain relief, for teething pain, or following an injury, in our locked medications drawer. For both circumstances you will need to complete the form: Parental Agreement for School to Administer Medicine
All administration of medication is recorded and if it is a non-prescribed medication you will receive a text, stating the dose and time your child received this.
If your child has asthma, please ask their GP to prescribe an additional inhaler that can be kept specifically in school. Children who can self-administer may keep their inhalers in class, or if they are younger or wish to use their inhaler discreetly, may keep their inhalers and spacers in the office. They will be shown where these are and kept in named individual bags with their photo and parental contact information. Access to inhalers kept in the school office is always open. We also have our own inhalers for emergency use if an inhaler is left at home or unusable, however, we require you to consent to use of this via the following form: Record of Consent for Use of Salbutamol Inhaler
Please ask at the school office if you have any questions about this.

Admissions
We are delighted you have taken an interest in our school!
This page provides useful information about how to apply for a place for your child.
If you would like to come and have a look around our school, please contact the school office to arrange an appointment on 01935 872430
Applying for a Place at St Andrew’s CE Primary School – Reception Year (2026)
If your child is due to start Reception year in September 2026, please complete an application via the following link: Starting School for the First Time.
The deadline for applications for Reception year in September 2026 is 15 January 2026.
Applying for a Place at St Andrew’s CE Primary School – In Year Transfers
If your child has already started school and you would like them to join us at St Andrew’s CE Primary School, you can apply for an In Year School Transfer at any time, via the following link: Applying for an In Year School Transfer
Need Help?
If you need help with a school application please contact our school office on 01935 872430 or office@yetminster.dorset.sch.uk
School Admission policy
The admission policy follows that laid down by the Sherborne Area Schools Trust (SAST). Our admissions (and selection) are conducted through our local authority based at Dorset County Council.
The children start at the beginning of the school year in which they are five. All children can start school full time, but parents can request part time arrangements for any period until the child reaches compulsory school age.
The school admission limit is 30 children per academic year and providing the year group is not oversubscribed then places can be offered to children living outside the catchment area.

Aims / Ethos
Nothing is impossible with God- Luke 1:37
Our Aims and Vision
Our aims are firmly rooted in our Christian Values, which provide a strong foundation for every child to grow into a responsible, compassionate citizen within an ever-changing global society. These values guide our decisions, shape our curriculum, and inspire our community to live with purpose and integrity.
As a proud member of the Sherborne Area Schools Trust (SAST), we share a common vision that permeates every aspect of school life: to nurture excellence, foster inclusivity, and prepare children for a future filled with opportunity.
An Inclusive Community
We are a fully inclusive Church of England School, welcoming families from all faiths and non-faith traditions. Our ethos is built on mutual respect and understanding, as we learn and work together for the betterment of our world. Diversity is celebrated, and every child is valued as a unique individual with limitless potential.
Our School Values
Love – We show kindness, respect, and compassion to all. Learn – We embrace curiosity and strive for excellence in all we do. Grow – We develop resilience, confidence, and a sense of responsibility. Flourish – We encourage creativity and joy, enabling every child to thrive.
Every aspect of school life is intrinsically linked to these values and their biblical underpinning. We believe that “Nothing is Impossible with God”, and this conviction drives us to serve our children and local community wholeheartedly.
Our Commitment to Every Child
Our ultimate aim is for every child to leave our school fully equipped with the skills, knowledge, and character they need for the next stage of their life adventure. We want them to be confident learners, compassionate friends, and courageous leaders who make a positive difference in the world.
